s: Which one of the following was a significant institutional outcome of the 1972 Stockholm Conference?
o: Creation of the Sustainable Development Goals
Adoption of the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation
x: The Stockholm Conference led to the establishment of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
tq: Identify the outcome associated with the correct summit rather than a later conference.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development?
x: The Future We Want was adopted at the 2012 Rio+20 Conference. Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, the UNFCCC and the CBD were associated with the 1992 Earth Summit.
tq: Use the summit-outcome association to eliminate the later document.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: The Rio Declaration adopted at the 1992 Earth Summit contained how many principles?
x: The Rio Declaration contains 27 principles relating to environment and development.
tq: Separate the numerical details of the Rio Declaration from SDG figures.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: The Johannesburg Plan of Implementation was the principal outcome document of:
o: The 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development
x: The Johannesburg Plan of Implementation was adopted at the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development.
tq: Match the named document with the summit that produced it.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the 2012 United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, consider the following statements:
1. It is popularly known as Rio+20.
2. It produced the document titled 'The Future We Want'.
3. It initiated the decision to frame the Sustainable Development Goals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The 2012 UNCSD at Rio de Janeiro was known as Rio+20, adopted The Future We Want and decided to frame the SDGs.
tq: Use the all-correct combination when the summit, document and institutional decision align.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: The 2015 United Nations Sustainable Development Summit was held in:
x: The 2015 UN Sustainable Development Summit was held in New York during the 70th session of the UN General Assembly.
tq: Distinguish the venue of the final SDG adoption summit from the Rio conferences.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: The document titled 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development' contains:
x: The 2030 Agenda contains 17 Sustainable Development Goals and 169 targets. It is also associated with 232 indicators.
tq: Separate goals, targets and indicators rather than interchanging their figures.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: The Sustainable Development Goals formally came into force from:
x: The 2030 Agenda and its SDGs were adopted in 2015 and came into force from 2016.
tq: Distinguish the adoption year from the year in which the framework became operational.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: Agenda 21 is best described as:
o: A comprehensive action plan for sustainable development at local, national and global levels
A statistical index ranking countries by sustainability
A legally binding treaty limited to climate change mitigation
A declaration containing only principles on biodiversity conservation
x: Agenda 21 is a comprehensive action plan for sustainable development at local, national and global levels.
tq: Choose the precise functional description rather than a related treaty or index.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the MDGs and SDGs?
o: The MDGs and SDGs were adopted in the same year.
The MDGs for 2000–2015 preceded the SDGs.
The MDGs replaced the 2030 Agenda after 2015.
x: The Millennium Development Goals covered 2000–2015 and preceded the Sustainable Development Goals under the 2030 Agenda.
tq: Use the time span to establish which global framework came first.
sec: Sustainable development summits - venue, formal UN name, outcome documents  [APPSC]

s: The report 'Our Common Future' was issued in which year?
x: The Brundtland Commission issued Our Common Future in 1987.
tq: Use the report-year association without confusing it with the Rio Summit year.
sec: Definition - Brundtland Commission report, year, chairperson, wording  [APPSC]

s: Which commission is credited with the first formal definition of sustainable development?
o: United Nations Commission on Human Settlements
World Trade Organization Commission on Development
World Commission on Environment and Development
International Union for Conservation of Nature Commission on Climate
x: The World Commission on Environment and Development, popularly called the Brundtland Commission, is credited with first defining sustainable development in Our Common Future.
tq: Identify the institution associated with the landmark definition.
sec: Definition - Brundtland Commission report, year, chairperson, wording  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly expresses the core temporal balance in the Brundtland definition of sustainable development?
o: Prohibiting the present generation from using natural resources
Meeting present needs while preserving future generations' ability to meet their needs
Giving priority exclusively to future generations over present needs
Maximising present economic growth regardless of environmental effects
x: The definition balances present needs with the ability of future generations to meet their own needs; it neither rejects development nor prohibits resource use.
tq: Test the exact balance in the definition rather than an extreme interpretation.
sec: Definition - Brundtland Commission report, year, chairperson, wording  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classic pillars of sustainable development?
x: The three classic pillars are economic development, social equity and environmental protection. Military security is not one of them.
tq: Identify the outsider from the standard three-pillar framework.
sec: Pillars of sustainable development - number, names, odd-one-out, triple bottom line  [APPSC]

s: The three pillars of sustainable development are intended to be:
o: Balanced and treated as interlinked dimensions
Replaced by political, military and cultural objectives
Pursued in isolation, with economic growth taking priority
x: Economic development, social equity and environmental protection are interlinked pillars that must be balanced rather than pursued in isolation.
tq: Reject the reversed comparison that gives one pillar absolute priority.
sec: Pillars of sustainable development - number, names, odd-one-out, triple bottom line  [APPSC]

s: In the business-oriented expression of sustainable development, the triple bottom line is represented by:
x: The triple bottom line is commonly expressed as People, Planet and Profit, corresponding broadly to social, environmental and economic concerns.
tq: Recall the exact three-part phrase used for the business version of sustainability.
sec: Pillars of sustainable development - number, names, odd-one-out, triple bottom line  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about principles of sustainable development:
1. Intergenerational equity requires the present generation to avoid depleting resources at the cost of future generations.
2. The precautionary principle permits postponement of preventive action until complete scientific certainty is available.
3. The polluter pays principle places the cost of preventing and controlling pollution on the polluter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The precautionary principle states that lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to postpone cost-effective preventive measures, making statement 2 false.
tq: Spot the statement that reverses the precautionary principle.
sec: Goals and principles - intergenerational equity, precautionary, polluter pays, carrying capacity  [APPSC]

s: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) implies that:
o: Responsibilities are shared, but developed nations carry greater duties
Only developing countries bear responsibility for environmental protection
All countries have identical environmental duties and identical capacities
Environmental duties are restricted to countries that caused no historical pollution
x: CBDR recognises shared responsibility while assigning greater duties to developed nations in view of their capacities and historical contribution.
tq: Discriminate between shared responsibility and identical responsibility.
sec: Goals and principles - intergenerational equity, precautionary, polluter pays, carrying capacity  [APPSC]

s: Human use of natural systems remains within carrying capacity when it:
o: Eliminates all human use of ecosystems
Exceeds the regenerative ability of ecosystems
Stays within what ecosystems can support
Maximises resource extraction in the present
x: Carrying capacity refers to the level of human use that ecosystems can support without losing their ability to function and regenerate.
tq: Apply the definition to distinguish sustainable use from overuse and non-use.
sec: Goals and principles - intergenerational equity, precautionary, polluter pays, carrying capacity  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT a goal or principle of sustainable development as generally recognised in environmental policy?
o: Maximising economic growth at any cost
x: Maximising economic growth at any cost conflicts with sustainable development, which requires balance among economic, social and environmental concerns.
tq: Use the absolute phrase at any cost to identify the incompatible objective.
sec: Goals and principles - intergenerational equity, precautionary, polluter pays, carrying capacity  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is consistent with the scope of sustainable development?
o: Running down natural capital to maximise current output
Excluding disadvantaged groups from development planning
Treating environmental protection and development as mutually exclusive
Meeting present needs while promoting equity within and across generations
x: Sustainable development includes meeting present needs, equity within and across generations, and inclusion. It rejects depletion of natural capital and the opposition of environment to development.
tq: Select the option that combines present needs, equity and inclusion.
sec: Scope statements - what the concept includes and excludes; resource use by the present generation  [APPSC]

s: The expression 'leave no one behind' in the context of sustainable development primarily emphasises:
o: Withdrawal of the state from development policy
x: Leave no one behind expresses the commitment to inclusion and equity in development outcomes.
tq: Translate the policy phrase into its underlying sustainable-development principle.
sec: Scope statements - what the concept includes and excludes; resource use by the present generation  [APPSC]

s: The National Environment Policy, 2006 treats conservation and livelihood security as:
o: Objectives that cannot be pursued together
Objectives applicable only to urban areas
x: The National Environment Policy, 2006 holds that conservation and livelihood security are linked rather than opposed.
tq: Watch for the reversed comparison between conservation and livelihoods.
sec: Scope statements - what the concept includes and excludes; resource use by the present generation  [APPSC]

s: Green GDP is obtained by:
o: Adding only gross industrial output to conventional GDP
Subtracting unpaid household work from GDP
Adjusting GDP for natural-resource depletion and environmental damage
Measuring only the value of protected forests
x: Green GDP adjusts conventional GDP to account for natural-resource depletion and environmental damage.
tq: Distinguish an environmentally adjusted economic measure from a social-progress indicator.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following best describes the Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI)?
o: It measures the date on which annual resource demand exceeds regeneration.
It is GDP without any adjustment for environmental factors.
It measures only the physical area of productive land used by a population.
It adds unpaid work and similar benefits while subtracting pollution, crime and resource loss.
x: GPI incorporates benefits such as unpaid work and deducts social and environmental costs including pollution, crime and resource loss.
tq: Match the indicator with both its additions and deductions.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: The ecological footprint of a population refers to the:
o: Annual date on which its natural resources are exhausted
Amount of carbon dioxide emitted by its industries alone
Productive land and sea needed to meet its consumption and absorb its wastes
Total number of endangered species in its territory
x: An ecological footprint estimates the productive land and sea area required to supply consumption and absorb generated wastes, expressed in global hectares.
tq: Use the function of the measure to distinguish it from emissions and biodiversity counts.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: The ecological footprint is expressed in:
x: Ecological footprint is measured in global hectares, representing biologically productive land and sea area.
tq: Recall the specialised unit associated with the footprint measure.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: Earth Overshoot Day is the date on which:
o: The global population reaches its carrying capacity permanently
All countries achieve their annual emissions targets
The annual production of renewable resources becomes zero
Humanity's demand exceeds what Earth can regenerate during that year
x: Earth Overshoot Day marks the point in a year when humanity's demand on ecological resources exceeds Earth's regenerative capacity for that year.
tq: Identify the event described by the date rather than confusing it with a target or permanent limit.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: According to the Sustainable Development Report 2025, India was ranked among how many countries in the SDG Index?
x: India ranked 99th out of 193 countries in the Sustainable Development Report 2025, entering the top 100 for the first time.
tq: Keep the rank and total number of countries together to avoid numerical substitution.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: Which organisation publishes the Sustainable Development Report associated with the SDG Index?
x: The Sustainable Development Report is published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (UN SDSN).
tq: Distinguish the international SDG Index publisher from India's domestic index institution.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the SDG indices mentioned for international and Indian assessment?
o: The Sustainable Development Report is associated with UN SDSN, while the SDG India Index ranks States through NITI Aayog.
UN SDSN ranks Indian States, while NITI Aayog ranks all countries.
The SDG India Index measures only biodiversity, while the Sustainable Development Report measures only climate change.
Both indices are prepared exclusively by the World Bank.
x: The Sustainable Development Report and its SDG Index are associated with UN SDSN, whereas NITI Aayog's SDG India Index ranks Indian States.
tq: Compare the authority and scope of the international and Indian indices.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s: The first edition of the Sustainable Development Report was published in:
x: The Sustainable Development Report was first published in 2016; the 2025 report is its tenth edition.
tq: Distinguish the first publication year from the adoption year of the SDGs.
sec: Measures - Green GDP, GPI, ecological footprint, Earth Overshoot Day  [other exams]

s:
Which of the following correctly presents the chronological order of the major precursors and milestones of the 2030 Agenda?
A. World Conservation Strategy
B. Brundtland Report
C. Rio Earth Summit
D. Agenda 2030/SDGs
x: The World Conservation Strategy was issued in 1980, followed by the Brundtland Report in 1987, the Rio Earth Summit in 1992 and Agenda 2030/SDGs in 2015.
tq: Arrange the milestones by their years before checking the options.
sec: Precursors - Limits to Growth, World Conservation Strategy, chronology to Agenda 2030

s: The report 'Limits to Growth' was associated with:
o: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
x: Limits to Growth was associated with the Club of Rome and appeared in 1972.
tq: Match the landmark report with its originating group.
sec: Precursors - Limits to Growth, World Conservation Strategy, chronology to Agenda 2030

s: The World Conservation Strategy of 1980 was prepared by which combination?
x: The 1980 World Conservation Strategy was associated with IUCN, UNEP and WWF and represented an early use of the term sustainable development.
tq: Start from the sure institutional trio to solve the association.
sec: Precursors - Limits to Growth, World Conservation Strategy, chronology to Agenda 2030

s: Which of the following milestones is correctly matched with its year?
x: The World Conservation Strategy was associated with 1980. Limits to Growth and the Rio Earth Summit belong to 1972 and 1992 respectively, while Agenda 2030 belongs to 2015.
tq: Check each year against the milestone before accepting the correctly matched pair.
sec: Precursors - Limits to Growth, World Conservation Strategy, chronology to Agenda 2030

s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Millennium Development Goals
B. Rio+20 Conference
C. World Summit on Sustainable Development at Johannesburg
D. Agenda 2030 and Sustainable Development Goals
x: The MDGs began in 2000, WSSD was held in 2002, Rio+20 in 2012 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
tq: Use the first and last milestones, then place the 2002 and 2012 events between them.
sec: Precursors - Limits to Growth, World Conservation Strategy, chronology to Agenda 2030

s: Which landmark judgment recognised sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle as part of Indian environmental law?
o: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
x: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996) recognised sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle in Indian environmental law.
tq: Identify the landmark judgment from the specific principles associated with it.
sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

s:
With reference to environmental jurisprudence in India, consider the following statements:
1. The polluter-pays principle was recognised in Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India.
2. The public trust doctrine was recognised in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath.
3. The precautionary principle was recognised in Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The 1996 Indian Council case affirmed polluter pays, the 1997 Kamal Nath case recognised the public trust doctrine, and the 1996 Vellore case recognised the precautionary principle.
tq: Match each case with its distinctive environmental-law principle.
sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

s:
The constitutional foundation for environmental protection in India includes which of the following provisions?
1. Article 21
2. Article 48A
3. Article 51A(g)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Articles 21, 48A and 51A(g) together constitute the constitutional base identified for environmental protection and sustainable development in India.
tq: Use the complete constitutional grouping rather than selecting only one category of provision.
sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal (NGT):
1. It is a statutory body established under the NGT Act, 2010.
2. It is a constitutional body created directly by the Constitution of India.
3. Its headquarters is at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The NGT is a statutory body under the NGT Act, 2010, and its headquarters is at New Delhi. It is not a constitutional body.
tq: Spot the wrong institutional classification by contrasting statutory and constitutional bodies.
sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

s: Which one of the following is NOT a bench location of the National Green Tribunal mentioned in the institutional arrangement?
x: The NGT benches mentioned are at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai. Hyderabad is not included in this list.
tq: Find the location that does not belong to the stated list of NGT benches.
sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

s: The National Green Tribunal is required to apply which combination of principles while adjudicating environmental cases?
o: Sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter-pays principle
Public trust doctrine, absolute liability and eminent domain
Common but differentiated responsibilities, prior appropriation and res judicata
Inter-generational equity, federal supremacy and parliamentary privilege
x: The NGT must apply the principles of sustainable development, precautionary action and polluter pays.
tq: Select the complete statutory-principle combination rather than a partly related doctrine.
sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

s: The principal aim of the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision is to make Andhra Pradesh a:

Carbon-neutral, Industrial and Export-oriented state by 2035

Wealthy, Healthy and Happy state by 2047

s: Which set of measures is associated with the Sustainability and Climate Resilience pillar of Swarna Andhra @2047?

Coal expansion, private transport and dispersed urbanisation
Nuclear energy, rural depopulation and industrial zoning
River diversion, road widening and conventional urban planning

s:
Consider the following statements regarding renewable energy under the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision:
1. Its contribution is approximately 30% at present.
2. The target is to increase the contribution to more than 75% by 2047.
3. The target is to keep the contribution below 50% by 2047.

x: Renewable energy contributes approximately 30% currently, with a target of more than 75% by 2047. Statement 3 reverses the stated target and is false.

s: The green-cover targets associated with Swarna Andhra @2047 are:

s: The AP-UN-Habitat Memorandum of Understanding of July 2026 envisages establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at:

s:

1. It relates to climate-resilient cities.
2. It is connected with Sustainable Development Goal 11.
3. It proposes a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes UN-Habitat?
o: It was set up in 1992 and has its headquarters at Amaravati.
It was set up in 1987 and has its headquarters at New Delhi.
It was set up in 1978 and has its headquarters at Nairobi.
It was set up in 1972 and has its headquarters at Geneva.

Wetlands, mangroves, deserts and coral reefs
